questions.question: What does a successful run of this lesson's stdlib harness prove?
options: The in-process policy and data flow behaved as asserted
A real MCP transport completed initialization
An OAuth authorization server issued a valid token
A collector received every OpenTelemetry span
questions.explanation: The harness uses Python functions, static tokens, fixtures, and in-memory spans. It validates those local boundaries while leaving protocol, authorization, export, browser, and sandbox integration to later tests.

questions.question: Which flow matches MCP revision 2026-07-28 for discovering a server and polling long-running work?
options: server/connect, tools/poll, tasks/status
server/discover, tools/call returning a task handle, tasks/get
initialize, tools/call, tasks/result
GET /mcp, tools/call, tasks/list
questions.explanation: The stateless revision uses mandatory `server/discover`. The optional `io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks` extension returns a task handle and uses `tasks/get`; a terminal task carries its final result. The old handshake, GET endpoint, `tasks/result`, and `tasks/list` are not in this flow.

questions.question: How does A2A v1 name the send-message operation in its gRPC and JSON-RPC bindings?
options: AgentMessage
message/create
tasks/send
SendMessage
questions.explanation: A2A v1 uses `SendMessage` for gRPC and JSON-RPC. Its HTTP+JSON binding exposes `POST /message:send`.

questions.question: Which MCP Apps SDK call lets an App request a tool on its originating server?
options: host.callTool(name, args)
app.callServerTool({ name, arguments })
app.invoke(name, args)
server.tools.call(args)
questions.explanation: The App instance calls `callServerTool` with an object containing `name` and optional `arguments`; the host proxies the underlying `tools/call` request.

questions.question: What authority does the capstone Agent Skill provide over MCP tools and the sandbox?
options: It bypasses approval after explicit invocation
It grants every tool named in the body
It grants read-only network access
None; host adapters and policy still authorize each capability
questions.explanation: A skill supplies procedure. Discovery, invocation, tool exposure, authorization, credentials, and isolation are enforced by the host and external runtime boundaries.

questions.question: Which evidence best proves that telemetry crossed the production export boundary?
options: A skill instruction saying to emit spans
A local dictionary containing a traceId key
A diagram of the intended span hierarchy
Receiver-side collector data with trace and parent assertions
questions.explanation: A receiver-side observation proves the SDK, propagator, exporter, transport, and collector path worked. Local data and diagrams prove only local construction or intent.
